The '''Pharmaceutical industry in Gujarat''' ranks number one in India with a 33% share in [[drug manufacturing]] and a 28% share in drug exports. The state has 130 [[USFDA]] certified [[drug manufacturing]] facilities.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-09-04 |title=Gujarat's pharma industry growth hits 'fever pitch' |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/gujarats-pharma-industry-growth-hits-fever-pitch/articleshow/103338812.cms |access-date=2023-09-04 |issn=0971-8257}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=June 2021 |title=Gujarat Pharma Industry – Vibrant Gujarat |url=https://vibrantgujarat.com/assets/img/Sectors/8.%20Pharmaceuticals%20and%20Medical%20Devices_June%2021.pdf |website=[[Vibrant Gujarat]] |access-date=6 April 2023 |archive-date=6 April 2023 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=29 September 2013 |title=Gujarat — pharmacy to the nation April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407031818/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/Gujarat-%E2%80%94-pharmacy-to-the-nation/article20670957.ece |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Gujarat]] is one of the major states in India and has a significant presence in the [[pharmaceutical industry]]. The state is home to several large pharmaceutical companies: [[Sun Pharma]]ceuticals ,[[Cadila Pharmaceuticals]], [[Torrent Pharmaceuticals]], [[Alembic Pharmaceuticals]], [[Intas Pharmaceuticals]], [[Zydus Lifesciences]], [[Amneal Pharmaceuticals]], USV Pharmaceuticals, [[Baxter International|Baxter]] Healthcare and Outsuka Pharma more.<ref>{{Cite news |date=7 August 2020 |title=Gujarat's pharma companies post net profit growth |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/states-top-pharma-cos-post-net-profit-growth/articleshow/77401498.cms |access-date=2023-04-05 |issn=0971-8257 |archive-date=9 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230409160334/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/states-top-pharma-cos-post-net-profit-growth/articleshow/77401498.cms |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dalal |first=Ravi Shah, Devanshi |date=11 September 2019 |title=Gujarat – A Re-emerging Pharma Destination? |url=https://corporate.cyrilamarchandblogs.com/2019/09/gujarat-a-reemerging-pharma-destination/ |access-date=2023-04-05 |website=India Corporate Law |language=en-US |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406203151/https://corporate.cyrilamarchandblogs.com/2019/09/gujarat-a-reemerging-pharma-destination/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Overview==
[[Gujarat]] has become a hub for the [[pharmaceutical industry]], with several established companies such as [[Torrent Pharmaceuticals]], [[Zydus Lifesciences]], [[Cadila Pharmaceuticals]], [[Alembic Pharmaceuticals]], [[Sun Pharma]], Claris, [[Intas Pharmaceuticals]], and [[Dishman Pharmaceuticals and Chemicals|Dishman Pharmaceuticals]] having operations in the state. Gujarat currently has around 5000 drug manufacturing units and contributes 42 percent of India's pharmaceutical turnover and 22 percent of its exports as of 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pharma Industry in Gujarat |url=https://btm.gujarat.gov.in/pharma-health-care-biotechnology.htm |website=GSBTM |access-date=6 April 2023 |archive-date=13 November 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191113070955/https://btm.gujarat.gov.in/pharma-health-care-biotechnology.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> Over 52,000 individuals are employed in Gujarat's pharmaceutical sector, which has experienced a [[Compound annual growth rate|Compound Annual Growth Rate]] (CAGR) of 54 percent in capital investments over the last three years.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=5 January 2008 |title=Gujarat Pharma Industry in 2008 – KPMG |url=http://www.in.kpmg.com/pdf/gujarat-pharma08.pdf |website=[[KPMG]] |access-date=6 April 2023 |archive-date=21 April 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150421102004/http://www.in.kpmg.com/pdf/gujarat-pharma08.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=6 January 2008 |title=Gujarat can emarge as global pharmaceutical hub: KPMG |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/pharmaceuticals/gujarat-can-emarge-as-global-pharmaceutical-hub-kpmg/articleshow/2678862.cms |access-date=2023-04-05 |issn=0013-0389 |archive-date=5 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230405164949/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/pharmaceuticals/gujarat-can-emarge-as-global-pharmaceutical-hub-kpmg/articleshow/2678862.cms |url-status=live }}</ref>

Gujarat's [[pharmaceutical industry]] holds a significant position in India, accounting for 40 percent of the country's total [[Pharmaceutical manufacturing|pharmaceutical production]] and 17 percent of its exports. The industry is valued at US$5.5 Billion.

==History==

* 1907: Alembic Pharmaceuticals, one of the oldest pharmaceutical companies in India, was established in [[Vadodara]], Gujarat. This was just six years after India's first domestic pharmaceutical unit, [[Bengal Chemicals and Pharmaceuticals|Bengal Chemical and Pharmaceutical Works]], was set up in [[Calcutta]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Alembic pharma history |url=https://wap.business-standard.com/company/alembic-pharma-40294/information/company-history |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=www.business-standard.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

During the 1940s and 50s, companies like The Gujarat Pharmaceutical and Chemical Works, Sarabhai Chemicals, Atul Products Ltd, Allied and Cadila Laboratories were established.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=How Gujarat Became the Pharma Hub of India |url=https://insider.finology.in/economy/gujarat-pharma-hub-of-india |access-date=2023-04-05 |website=insider.finology.in |language=en |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406102618/https://insider.finology.in/economy/gujarat-pharma-hub-of-india |url-status=live }}</ref>

* 1947: The Drugs Laboratory in Vadodara was established, followed by LM College of Pharmacy.<ref>{{Cite web |title=L. M. College of Pharmacy |url=https://lmcp.ac.in/governance/ |access-date=2023-04-05 |language=en-US |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406101458/https://lmcp.ac.in/governance/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":0" />
* 1989: The B.V. Patel Education Trust, [[Ahmedabad]] and Gujarat Branch of Indian Pharmaceutical Association (IPA) established the B.V. Patel Pharmaceutical Education and Research Development (PERD) Centre in Ahmedabad.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pharma machinery units foraying into new markets |url=http://test.pharmabiz.com/chronicle%20specials/pharma-machinery-units-foraying-into-new-markets-99396 |access-date=2023-04-05 |website=test.pharmabiz.com |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406220258/http://test.pharmabiz.com/chronicle%20specials/pharma-machinery-units-foraying-into-new-markets-99396 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Over the years, the pharmaceutical industry in Gujarat has grown significantly. The invested capital to labor ratio has risen significantly and the employment rate has almost doubled between 1979 and 1980 and 1997–98. There are currently around 3,500 drug manufacturing units in Gujarat, which employ over 52,000 individuals.<ref name=":1" />

* 2000: The [[Government of Gujarat]] declared the state a "pharma hub" and initiated several measures to promote the growth of the industry.
* 2003: Torrent Pharmaceuticals, one of the leading pharmaceutical companies in Gujarat, received US [[FDA approval]] for its manufacturing facilities.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Torrent Pharma Share Price Today(06 Apr, 2023) – Torrent Pharma Share Price Live NSE/BSE |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/torrent-pharmaceuticals-ltd/stocks/companyid-8492.cms |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=The Economic Times |language=en |archive-date=7 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230607214106/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/torrent-pharmaceuticals-ltd/stocks/companyid-8492.cms |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Company News: Company Business News, Indian Companies News, Company Analysis, Corporate Industry News |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331115713/https://www.business-standard.com/companies |archive-date=31 March 2023 |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=www.business-standard.com |language=en-US}}</ref>
* 2005: Alembic Pharmaceuticals, another major pharmaceutical company in Gujarat, received US FDA approval for its manufacturing facilities.<ref>{{Cite web |date= |title=Alembic Pharmaceuticals 2006 |url=https://www.alembiclimited.com/Annual_Report/al-05-06.pdf |website=[[Alembic Pharmaceuticals]] |access-date=6 April 2023 |archive-date=30 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230530114317/https://www.alembiclimited.com/Annual_Report/al-05-06.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Research and Development ==
The pharmaceutical sector in [[Gujarat]] has a significant focus on [[research and development]] (R&D), which has contributed to the growth of the industry in the state. The state government has been actively promoting [[R&D]] in the pharmaceutical sector and has established a number of initiatives to support this.

Gujarat FDCA (Food and Drugs Control Administration) Innovation and Research Cell, which was established to promote [[R&D]] in the pharmaceutical industry. The cell provides support for R&D activities and facilitates collaborations between the industry and academia.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FDCA |url=https://ayudmla.gujarat.gov.in/home.php |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=ayudmla.gujarat.gov.in |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406091104/https://ayudmla.gujarat.gov.in/home.php |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=fdca: Latest News & Videos, Photos about fdca   |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/fdca |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=The Economic Times |language=en |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406091102/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/fdca |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Network |first=eHealth |date=1 September 2017 |title=E-initiatives by Gujarat FDCA Revolutionising the Drug Sector in India – Elets eHealth |url=https://ehealth.eletsonline.com/2017/09/e-initiatives-by-gujarat-fdca-revolutionising-the-drug-sector-in-india/ |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=eHealth Magazine |language=en-US |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406091104/https://ehealth.eletsonline.com/2017/09/e-initiatives-by-gujarat-fdca-revolutionising-the-drug-sector-in-india/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In addition, the state government has established the Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre (GBRC) to promote [[biotechnology]] research in the state. The centre provides infrastructure and technical support to [[research institutions]] and companies in the biotechnology sector.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre |url=https://gbrc.gujarat.gov.in/ |website=GBRC |access-date=6 April 2023 |archive-date=28 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250328174335/https://gbrc.gujarat.gov.in/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=gujarat biotechnology research centre: Latest News & Videos, Photos about gujarat biotechnology research centre   |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/gujarat-biotechnology-research-centre |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=The Economic Times |language=en |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406091932/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/gujarat-biotechnology-research-centre |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=14 March 2021 |title=Gujarat Biotechnology Research Center contributes to Covid genomes sequencing |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/gujarat-biotechnology-research-center-contributes-to-covid-genomes-sequencing-7227302/ |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=The Indian Express |language=en |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406091932/https://indianexpress.com/article/india/gujarat-biotechnology-research-center-contributes-to-covid-genomes-sequencing-7227302/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The Gujarat government has also established several science and [[Science park|technology parks]] in the state, including the [[Gujarat Science City]] in Ahmedabad<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gujarat Science City |url=https://sciencecity.gujarat.gov.in/ |website=[[Gujarat Science City]] |access-date=6 April 2023 |archive-date=27 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230327074418/https://sciencecity.gujarat.gov.in/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and the Gujarat Biotech Park in Vadodara. These parks provide infrastructure and support services to companies engaged in R&D activities in various sectors, including pharmaceuticals.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rs 2000 cr Gujarat Biotech Park at Vadodara likely to be launched in April |url=http://test.pharmabiz.com/news/rs-2000-cr-gujarat-biotech-park-at-vadodara-likely-to-be-launched-in-april-43855 |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=test.pharmabiz.com |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406095706/http://test.pharmabiz.com/news/rs-2000-cr-gujarat-biotech-park-at-vadodara-likely-to-be-launched-in-april-43855 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Gujarat State Biotechnology Mission (GSBTM), Savli Biotech Park {{!}} India Science, Technology & Innovation – ISTI Portal |url=https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/technologyincubators/gujarat-state-biotechnology-mission-gsbtm-savli-biotech-park |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406101209/https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/technologyincubators/gujarat-state-biotechnology-mission-gsbtm-savli-biotech-park |url-status=live }}</ref>

Many of the leading pharmaceutical companies in Gujarat have their own [[R&D]] facilities and are actively engaged in the development of new products and technologies. For example, Zydus Lifesciences and Intas Pharmaceuticals one of the largest pharmaceutical companies in Gujarat, has a state-of-the-art R&D facility in [[Ahmedabad]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zydus pharma Research Center {{!}} Vaccine Technology Centre in India |url=https://zyduslife.com/research |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=zyduslife.com |language=en |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406100250/https://zyduslife.com/research |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=R & D – Intas Pharmaceuticals Ltd. |url=https://www.intaspharma.com/research-and-developement/ |access-date=2023-04-06 |language=en-US |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406100741/https://www.intaspharma.com/research-and-developement/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Similarly, Torrent Pharmaceuticals has a dedicated R&D centre in [[Gandhinagar]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Torrent Pharmaceuticals |url=https://www.torrentpharma.com/index.php/site/info/rnd |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=www.torrentpharma.com |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406100251/https://www.torrentpharma.com/index.php/site/info/rnd |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=28 February 2022 |title=Indian pharma firms look to ramp up investments in R&D, innovation |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/industry/pharma/story/indian-pharma-firms-look-to-ramp-up-investments-in-rd-innovation-324194-2022-02-28 |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=Business Today |language=hi |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406100248/https://www.businesstoday.in/industry/pharma/story/indian-pharma-firms-look-to-ramp-up-investments-in-rd-innovation-324194-2022-02-28 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In addition to the initiatives and facilities mentioned earlier, the Gujarat government has also established the [[National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research, Ahmedabad|National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research]] to promote [[R&D]] in the pharmaceutical sector. The centre provides infrastructure and [[technical support]] to pharmaceutical companies and [[research institutions]] in the state. It also facilitates collaborations between the industry and academia, and encourages the commercialization of R&D outcomes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education & Research |url=https://www.niperahm.ac.in/ |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=www.niperahm.ac.in |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406100740/https://www.niperahm.ac.in/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The [[Government of Gujarat|state government]] has also established a number of policies and [[incentive]]s to promote R&D in the pharmaceutical sector. For example, the Gujarat Industrial Policy 2020 provides various incentives to companies engaged in [[R&D]] activities, including subsidies for the development of new products, [[tax exemption]]s on R&D expenditure, and funding for collaborations with [[academic institution]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gujarat Industrial Policy 2020 |url=https://ic.gujarat.gov.in/industrial-policy2020.aspx |website=ic.gujarat.gov.in |access-date=6 April 2023 |archive-date=12 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220712222352/https://ic.gujarat.gov.in/industrial-policy2020.aspx |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Vijay Rupani: Gujarat announces Industrial Policy 2020, CM Vijay Rupani says it will make the state Atmanirbhar – The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/policy/gujarat-announces-industrial-policy-2020-cm-vijay-rupani-says-it-will-make-the-state-atmanirbhar/articleshow/77410785.cms |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=[[The Economic Times]] |archive-date=8 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230408040014/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/policy/gujarat-announces-industrial-policy-2020-cm-vijay-rupani-says-it-will-make-the-state-atmanirbhar/articleshow/77410785.cms |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Gujarat government]] has taken the initiative to provide training in areas such as [[R&D]], manufacturing, quality control, and regulatory affairs, and aims to develop a skilled workforce for the industry.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gujarat FDCA to collaborate with PERD Centre to train drug regulators on soft skills, analytical techniques |url=http://www.pharmabiz.com/NewsDetails.aspx?aid=109870&sid=1 |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=www.pharmabiz.com |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406101542/http://www.pharmabiz.com/NewsDetails.aspx?aid=109870&sid=1 |url-status=live }}</ref>

the government initiatives, [[policies]], and [[incentive]]s have created an environment that promotes [[R&D]] in the pharmaceutical sector in [[Gujarat]]. This has led to the development of innovative products and technologies, which has helped to establish Gujarat as a hub for the pharmaceutical industry in India.<ref name=":2" />

== Exports ==
Gujarat is one of the leading states in [[India]] in terms of pharmaceutical exports. The state has a well-established pharmaceutical industry with a strong focus on quality and innovation, which has helped it to become a major exporter of pharmaceutical products. According to the data from the [[Ministry of Commerce and Industry]], Government of India, Gujarat was the second-largest exporter of pharmaceuticals in India during the fiscal year 2020–21, accounting for around 20% of the country's total pharmaceutical exports.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Department of Pharmaceuticals 2020–21 |url=https://pharmaceuticals.gov.in/sites/default/files/english%20Annual%20Report%202020-21.pdf |website=Department of Pharmaceuticals |access-date=6 April 2023 |archive-date=6 April 2023 Pharmaceutical exports from [[Gujarat]], India have increased by 11% in fiscal year 2018–19, according to data provided by the Gujarat State Board of Indian Drug Manufacturers’ Association (IDMA). Gujarat accounts for a minimum of 28% of India's pharma exports, with exports totalling $5.36bn in 2018–19, up from $4.83bn the previous year. The Indian pharma industry has bounced back with an estimated export value of $19.15bn in 2018–19, an increase of 10.85% over the previous year. The sector's strong performance is partly attributed to the strengthening of the dollar against the rupee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pharma exports from Gujarat grow exponentially |url=https://www.thepharmaletter.com/article/pharma-exports-from-gujarat-grow-exponentially |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=www.thepharmaletter.com |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406103018/https://www.thepharmaletter.com/article/pharma-exports-from-gujarat-grow-exponentially |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=7 January 2017 |title=Gujarat witnesses exponential growth in pharma exports |url=https://www.business-standard.com/amp/amp/article/companies/gujarat-witnesses-exponential-growth-in-pharma-exports-117010700788_1.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406104510/https://www.business-standard.com/amp/amp/article/companies/gujarat-witnesses-exponential-growth-in-pharma-exports-117010700788_1.html |archive-date=6 April 2023 |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=www.business-standard.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=10 April 2019 |title=Pharma exports from Gujarat rise 11% in FY19 |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/pharma-exports-from-gujarat-rise-11-in-fy19/articleshow/68802254.cms |access-date=2023-04-06 |issn=0971-8257 |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406102608/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/pharma-exports-from-gujarat-rise-11-in-fy19/articleshow/68802254.cms |url-status=live }}</ref>

Gujarat's pharmaceutical exports consist of various types of products, including formulations, bulk drugs, intermediates, and [[drug formulation]]s. The major markets for Gujarat's pharmaceutical exports are the United States, [[European Union]], Africa, and the Middle East.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pharmaceutical industry, Pharmaceutical Exports from India- IBEF |url=https://www.ibef.org/exports/pharmaceutical-exports-from-india |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=India Brand Equity Foundation |language=en |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406103010/https://www.ibef.org/exports/pharmaceutical-exports-from-india |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Export Products (Pharmaceuticals) |url=https://commerce.gov.in/about-us/divisions/export-products-division/export-products-pharmaceuticals/ |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=Mcommerce |language=en |archive-date=6 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406103012/https://commerce.gov.in/about-us/divisions/export-products-division/export-products-pharmaceuticals/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The Pharmaceutical industry in Gujarat ranks number one in India with a 33% share in drug manufacturing and a 28% share in drug exports. The state has 130 USFDA certified drug manufacturing facilities. Ahmedabad and Vadodara are considered as pharmaceutical hubs as there are many big and small pharma companies established in these cities.
Gujarat is one of the major states in India and has a significant presence in the pharmaceutical industry. The state is home to several large pharmaceutical companies: Sun Pharmaceuticals ,Cadila Pharmaceuticals, Torrent Pharmaceuticals, Alembic Pharmaceuticals, Intas Pharmaceuticals, Zydus Lifesciences, Amneal Pharmaceuticals, USV Pharmaceuticals, Baxter Healthcare and Outsuka Pharma more.
